The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 26.01.2024.
2.
The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 26.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., petitioner was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.

No. KA-01-AH-4178, along with passenger near HP Petrol Bunk, OM Road, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru slowly cautiously and observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time all of a sudden a Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner's auto-rickshaw from behind.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food,
transport and other charges.

entities.text: MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 26 years, the petitioner was working as a Driver and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements.
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car.

sentences.text: Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was in-force as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it is contended that, as per the discharge summary of the MVJ Hospital, petitioner's auto toppled and not hit by Car, so it is a false case, there is actionable negligence on the part of the petitioner at the time of the accident.
Further this respondent No.1 submits that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the accident is occurred on the negligence of the petitioner.
Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 26.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., accident took place near HP Petrol Bunk, OM Road, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410 as a result the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13 and examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.14 and 15 and also examined MRD In-charge at MVJ Medical College and Hospital as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:

ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 26.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m.,
petitioner was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AH-4178, along with passenger near HP Petrol Bunk, OM Road, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru slowly cautiously and observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time all of a sudden a Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner's auto- rickshaw from behind.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru,
wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote, wherein he was treated as inpatient.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.28/2024.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".

On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 28/2024.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.

The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama and Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/

The Ex.P.5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
15.

In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of PW.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote, wherein he was treated as inpatient and he took treatment.

entities.text: MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
18. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 27.01.2024 to 28.01.2024.

entities.text: MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the MVJ Hospital, Hoskote for 01 day.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6,
which reveals that, petitioner has sustained abrasion over left elbow and tenderness over left shoulder and the doctor has opined that the injury is simple in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 09 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10 to the tune of Rs.8,456/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,456/- towards medical expenses.

20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9 Discharge summaries issued by MVJ Hospital, Hoskote, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 27.01.2024 to 28.01.2024 i.e. for 01 day.
Hence, at least 1 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contended that, the injured Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/
5 petitioner was a driver and earning Rs.40,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document before this court.

entities.text: Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally.
It is pertinent to note that, Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority framed chart of notional income and directed to follow the same.
As per the said guidelines, the fixed notional income for the year 2024 is at Rs.16,500/-.
Hence, 1 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head.
21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has deposed that, petitioner has sustained left clavicle fracture and opined that, total physical disability of the left arm at 30% and that of whole body disability at 10%.
Admittedly, PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
Learned counsel for petitioner argued that, petitioner sustained left Clavicle fracture and he has taken treatment for the same.
Further he argued that, due to the said injury petitioner is unable to drive his auto-rickshaw.
Hence, requested to consider 10% disability.
In support of his argument he relied upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 1556/2016 between Ramachandra Vs. Girija. K and another.

entities.text: Ramachandra Vs. Girija. K and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On going through the above Judgment wherein, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in similar circumstances upheld the award passed by the Tribunal for considering the disability to an extent of 5%.
But in the said Judgment also the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that, the Clavicle bone is an ornamental bone, the fracture of Clavicle bone does not amount to any disability.
Learned Counsel for insurance company argued that, the clavicle bone is only an ornamental bone and the said fracture does not lead to any disability.

In support of his argument he relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 1602/2016 between Jayanath Kumbar Vs M J Mahesha and another, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, clavicle bone is only an ornamental bone and the fracture does not lead to any disability.

entities.text: Jayanath Kumbar Vs M J Mahesha and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said observation in the above judgment is aptly applicable to the present case and moreover in this case petitioner was treated conservatively and he has not undergone any surgery.
It is relevant to note that, Clavicle or collar bone is as lender 'S' shaped bone approximately 6 inches that serves as strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.

Together with the shoulder blade,
it makes up the shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India Guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 10% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Accordingly, no grounds are made out to show that the said injury caused the permanent disability and economical loss to the petitioner.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 8,456/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 16,500/-
up period 4 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges Total Rs. 1,04,956/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,04,956/- under various heads.
23. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 09.12.2023 to 08.12.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 26.01.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
24. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
25. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
